[tool: bash]
I've written `polyglot/main.rs`, and both commands build and give the same answers: f(0)=1, f(1)=1, f(2)=2, f(3)=3, f(10)=89, f(100)=573147844013817084101.

**How it works:** the file relies on a difference in how comments behave in each language.
- **Rust** lets `/* ... */` comments nest, so `/* /* */` opens a comment that stays open. Rust skips everything up to the matching `// */` and compiles only the Rust code below it.
- **C++** doesn't nest comments, so `/* /* */` is just one complete comment. g++ compiles the C++ code that follows. The Rust part sits inside `#if 0 ... #endif`, so g++ ignores it.
- At the end of the file, a matching `/* /* */ ... // */` pair closes things off cleanly for both compilers.

Both versions do whole-number addition on numbers stored as chunks of 9 digits, so results don't overflow for large N (I tested up to N=200). If you run either program without an N, it prints a usage message and exits with code 1.
